target_customer: Hobbyist and aspiring webcomic creators who cannot draw, plus readers who pay per episode
problem: Webcomic platforms are limited by creators who can draw. Storyboarder wanted to let anyone build scenes, pose 3D characters and publish episodes as webcomics.
business_model: Creator platform with transaction fees on paid webcomic episodes (readers pay after a free set of episodes)
product_category: Webcomic creation tool and publishing marketplace

founders.name: Charles Forman
previous_startups: OMGPOP (YC S06, maker of Draw Something, acquired by Zynga)
founders.background_notes: YC page and launch post describe him as creator of the original open source Storyboarder tool while working on film. Education not found.

founders.name: Joe Watkins
founders.background_notes: YC page says he led a computer vision and machine learning team at Google and later worked on ML map generation at Waymo. Education not found.

competitors.name: Webtoon (Naver)
competitors.what: Largest webcomic platform, the incumbent that Storyboarder pitched against
competitors.traction_then: YC launch post cites about $1.2B annual revenue, while the YC page text says $100M per month, so the figure is inconsistent
competitors.funding_then: Part of Naver, not separately sourced

technical_complexity.rationale: A 3D posing and panel generation editor on top of an existing desktop storyboarding tool with roughly 650K users, plus a publishing and payment layer. Standard engineering with hard 3D and UX parts for a team of two.

defensibility.rationale: The installed base of storyboard tool users was a small head start, but the publishing marketplace had no network effect yet and tool features were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found of an incumbent copying the wedge. Many AI comic makers appeared after 2023 but none are dated near the batch.

market_need_then: YC page cites a $12B East Asian webcomic market growing worldwide and says readers want more story variety. Evidence of demand from creators who cannot draw is the founders' claim, with no independent source.

branding.domain_note: storyboarder.com returned a 301 redirect to sumugi.com when fetched in November 2026, so the exact domain no longer serves the Storyboarder brand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and creator oriented; Sumugi site uses the tagline Make Comics without drawing

rebrands.why: Not stated; inferred from domain redirect and a directory listing saying the platform was previously called Storyboarder. Copyright line still reads Storyboarder Inc.

branding.community_and_virality: The original open source Storyboarder tool had a GitHub community and press from film and tech outlets in 2017, and the YC page claims 650K to 700K users, but no sources show meme or merch activity.

brand_strength.rationale: The descriptive name was known among filmmakers as a free tool, but it was generic for webcomics and the company later moved to a different public name.

pivots.why: Founders say they want to democratize visual storytelling; YC launch March 2023

outcome_analysis: Storyboarder entered YC W23 with an existing storyboarding tool of about 650K users and a notable founder from OMGPOP, then pitched a webcomic platform. No funding amount is confirmed by a primary source, no exit is reported, and the web domain now redirects to a product called Sumugi from Storyboarder Inc, so the company appears to have continued under a new brand. The outcome is unclear, with no public traction figures after 2023.
notes: Funding: aggregators (CB Insights, extruct, vcbacked) report about $500K pre-seed with Y Combinator and Liquid 2 Ventures, but only one-snippet or aggregator sources, so unverified and not recorded as a round. YC page names angels David Karp, Andrew Kortina, Jonathan Glick and Andy Artz as investors without amounts. Headquarters and founding year conflict across aggregators. No dated competitor near the batch beyond Webtoon was found; later AI comic tools (Tooning, LlamaGen, Dashtoon) are from 2024 or later and are excluded. Completeness pass: one round recorded on the strength of a single database or outlet, CB Insights and VCBacked (databases only; CB Insights labels it seed). No primary announcement found.
